text:
Utah outplayed Edmonton and lost by four. The Mammoth won the expected goals count 2.78 to 2.15, outattempted the Oilers 62 to 45, and by the deserved-to-win measure took 61 percent of the simulated replays. None of it showed on the scoreboard, because Edmonton turned modest chances into goals while Utah's goaltending gave up far more than the shots called for.

Edmonton scored three times in the first period and twice more in the second, five goals on chances worth between 11 and 22 percent apiece. Connor McDavid started it at 00:40 with a backhand, Zach Hyman scored on the power play, and Mathieu Joseph made it 3-0 just 32 seconds later. Karel Vejmelka faced 17 shots and allowed five, 3.4 goals more than those shots deserved. Sebastian Cossa had been pulled after four shots and one goal. At the other end, Tristan Jarry stopped 26 of 28.

Utah's best stretch came too late. The third period belonged to the Mammoth, 1.12 to 0.48 in expected goals, and John Marino (a 5 percent chance) and Mikhail Sergachev scored 1:35 apart to make it 5-2. McDavid answered at 10:17 with his second goal of the night, a 21 percent snap shot, and finished with five points. Utah took the first meeting two days earlier, 4-2, but this time the finishing went the other way.
